terms.comment: Cicero also uses it as a deponent, pūnior, pūnīrī (Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: correct, punish (a child, a pupil); scold
evidence: Cic. Tusc. 3.64: puerōs nōn verbīs sōlum, sed etiam verberibus (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: To set right by word or deed, as a parent or a teacher does (Lewis & Short).

terms.grammar: phrase: poena, poenae f. (penalty) with afficere and the accusative of the person
phrase: poena, poenae f. (penalty) with dare
terms.comment: The usual way to say ‘be punished’: one pays the penalty. Also poenās solvere, pendere (Lewis & Short).

phrases.english: you’ll pay for it, I won’t say how

phrases.latin: sed majōrum nūgae negōtia vocantur, puerōrum autem tālia cum sint, pūniuntur ā majōribus
phrases.english: but the games of grown-ups are called business, and children’s, though they are just the same, are punished by grown-ups

phrases.latin: nam quō saepius monuerit, hōc rārius castīgābit
phrases.english: for the more often he warns, the less often he will have to punish
